beats.intro: Module nine. [[sub]]How interest rates change with maturity: spot, par, and forward curves.
beats.spot: So far we discounted every cash flow at one rate. But rates differ by maturity. [[ideal]]The ideal data are yields on default-risk-free zero-coupon bonds. They are spot rates, and together they form the spot curve. With no coupons, there is no reinvestment risk, and the bonds share the same currency, credit, and liquidity. [[shape]]Usually the spot curve slopes upward, and flattens for long maturities. [[inv]]Sometimes short rates exceed long rates. That is an inverted curve. [[prac]]In practice, spot curves are built from recently issued government coupon bonds, and filled in by interpolation.
beats.price: Spot rates price any bond. [[ex]]Take a three year bond with a five percent annual coupon. The spot rates are two, three, and four percent. [[each]]Discount each cash flow at its own spot rate. [[p1]]The first coupon is worth four point nine oh two. [[p2]]The second, four point seven one three. [[p3]]The final payment, one hundred five, is worth ninety three point three four five. [[sum]]The price is one hundred two point nine six. [[ytm]]Solving for the single rate that gives the same price gives a yield to maturity of three point nine three five percent. Different discounting, same price.
beats.par: A par rate is the yield that prices a bond at par. [[def]]It is derived from the spot rates up to that maturity. [[how]]The par rate equals one minus the final discount factor, divided by the sum of all the discount factors. [[ex]]With spot rates of two, three, and four percent, the par rates are two percent, two point nine nine, and three point nine five. [[note]]On an upward sloping curve, par rates sit below spot rates. Published government par curves, like the Treasury yield curve, are made of par rates.
beats.forward: A forward rate is the rate for a period that starts in the future. [[def]]It is implied by spot rates. Investing for three years must give the same result as investing for two years, and then rolling over at the forward rate. [[eq]]One plus the three year spot, cubed, equals one plus the two year spot, squared, times one plus the forward rate. [[ex]]With our spot rates, one point oh four cubed is one point one two four nine. One point oh three squared is one point oh six oh nine. So the one year forward rate, two years from now, is six point oh three percent. [[also]]Likewise, the one year rate, one year from now, is four point oh one percent. [[use]]A forward rate is the marginal return from extending the maturity by one more period.
beats.curves: Now compare the three curves. [[spot]]Here is an upward sloping spot curve. [[par]]The par curve is below it. [[fwd]]And the forward curve, the one year rate for each future year, is above it. [[inv]]For a downward sloping spot curve, it reverses. Par rates are above spot rates, and forward rates are below. [[why]]When the spot curve rises, each extra year must pay more than the average so far.
beats.wrap: Let's recap. [[w1]]Spot rates are zero-coupon yields, and each cash flow is discounted at its own spot rate. [[w2]]A par rate is the yield that prices a bond at par. [[w3]]Forward rates are implied by spot rates, and are marginal returns. [[w4]]On an upward curve, forward rates exceed spot rates, which exceed par rates. On a downward curve, the order reverses.
